entities.summary: Augustine of Canterbury, a 6th-century Benedictine monk known as the "Apostle to the English," was the first Archbishop of Canterbury and a founder of the English Church. Commissioned by Pope Gregory the Great, he established his seat in Kent after converting King Æthelberht and initiating the conversion of the Anglo-Saxons.
